evidence: Quint. 1.4.20: corpus vīsū tāctūque manifestum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The sense of sight, and a look or glance; also a thing seen, an apparition (see vision, in a dream).

evidence: Caes. B.G. 1.39: nē vultum quidem atque aciem oculōrum ferre potuisse (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: aciēs is an edge, the sharpness of a blade, and so the sharpness of the eyes; also, alone, the eyesight (Lucretius). Its commonest sense is a line of battle (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a look, sight; the range of sight
terms.comment: The act of looking and the power of seeing; also the way something looks, its appearance.

phrases.english: a body that sight and touch make plain

phrases.latin: Perspicilla, ut ācrius cernat, quī habet vīsum dēbilem.
phrases.english: Spectacles, so that someone with weak sight may see more sharply.
phrases.source: Comen. OP 79 (perspicillum is a modern word)

sources: Lewis & Short: visus · Lewis & Short: acies · Lewis & Short: aspectus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. vision, eyesight.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-comenius), checked against the editions named there. Quintilian and Caesar as Lewis & Short quotes them.
